subject: Locality proof and snapshot expunction — operational evidence request
messages:
From: Natalie Park <natalie.park@greenbank.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: cloudops@greenbank.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: locality proof & snapshot expunction for Dedicated cluster

Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking this — GreenBank is validating that data for our Dedicated tenant (tenant id: GNB-1876) is strictly constrained to the us-east-2 region and that any snapshots, cache artifacts, and ephemeral stores associated with the tenant can be reliably purged on request. We need: 

- A short ops attestation describing how region pinning is enforced for Dedicated (what prevents cross-region replication).
- An example snapshot manifest (redacted) showing storage location and retention TTL for a tenant snapshot.
- The standard deletion/expunction workflow for snapshots & cached KV (including timing and verification steps).
- Evidence artifacts you can share: audit entries, job IDs showing deletion execution, and a sample post-wipe verification (log excerpt).

For context: this is part of an upcoming GLBA review. We don’t need raw payloads, but we do need precise metadata and verification steps. Attached is our retention requirements PDF. Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide redacted manifests and a runbook excerpt within 5 business days? Also let us know if you require an HSR/POC for a live walkthrough.

Thanks,
Natalie Park
Director, Security Engineering
GreenBank Financial

Attachment: GNB-data-retention-reqs.pdf
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Park <natalie.park@greenbank.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: locality proof & snapshot expunction for Dedicated cluster

Hi Natalie — thanks for the clear list. We can provide the artifacts and a short attestation; high-level response below and an ETA.

What we will provide (redacted where required):
- Ops attestation (PDF) describing our region-pin enforcement and non-replication guarantees for Dedicated deployments.
- Redacted snapshot manifest CSV (bucket path prefix, object ids, size, created_at, TTL).
- Wipe/expunction playbook excerpt (steps used by production ops to remove tenant snapshots and evacuate KV caches).
- Audit log extracts and the wipe job IDs that show successful execution; we will include verification hashes where applicable.

Timeline: we can assemble redacted artifacts and the attestation within 4 business days. If you prefer a live walkthrough (30–45 min), we can schedule one the week after artifacts land.

Clarifying notes/questions:
1) Do you need KMS key identifiers included in the manifest, or should those be redacted?
2) For post-wipe verification, do you require only storage-layer evidence (S3-like object metadata + delete tombstones), or do you also want evidence from our inference runtime (cache invalidation logs, KV evict events)?

I’m looping in Laura from Ops and Ben from Product to make sure we pull the right artifacts and redact appropriately.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Senior Manager, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

Attachment: locality_evidence_checklist.xlsx
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, Natalie Park <natalie.park@greenbank.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: locality proof & snapshot expunction for Dedicated cluster

Hi Natalie / team — adding the ops detail you asked for and the specific artifacts we’ll pull. Quoting Olga’s note above.

Operational summary (concise):
- Region pinning: Dedicated clusters are deployed to region-specific tenancy pools. Control plane sets a "region_pin" flag at provisioning that disables cross-region replication for that tenant. Replication jobs check that flag before any snapshot copy.
- Snapshot handling: Snapshots are optional for Dedicated; by default we keep a single point-in-time snapshot for disaster recovery with a tenant-configured TTL (default 30 days). When a snapshot delete is requested, we mark snapshot objects for deletion and run a scrub job that removes objects and their manifests from storage. Deletion is executed as a job (wipe-job-id) and is recorded in the audit log.
- Ephemeral cache: KV prefix caches are TTL'd and also have a manual eviction endpoint. Cache evictions are recorded (evict-event-id) and we can provide sample log lines.
- Backup replication: For Dedicated, cross-region backup replication is off by default unless explicitly enabled in the customer's deployment contract.

Artifacts we will attach (redacted):
- dedicated-wipe-playbook.md — playbook sections (commands, expected audit entries, verification checklist).
- snapshot-manifest-20270520.csv — redacted manifest with bucket prefix, object ids (hashed), created_at, size, TTL.
- sample_audit_extract.log — lines showing wipe-job-id and verification steps.

Important: we will not include unencrypted payloads. KMS identifiers can be provided as a key alias if you need KMS confirmation (please indicate).

Internal note: Ops ticket OPS-4821 will be used to collect the artifacts and run the scrub in a staging tenant for demonstration.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Site Reliability
Redwood Inference

Thanks — that plan sounds good and the timeline is acceptable. A couple quick clarifications before you assemble artifacts: 

- Please include whether snapshots are encrypted with a customer-managed key (CMK) or a Redwood-managed key; we need to document key ownership for GLBA evidence. If CMK is used, we’ll want the alias (not the raw key).
- For the redacted manifest, please replace object ids with stable hashes (sha256) and include a short note on how we can verify deletion after the scrub (example audit lines are fine).

We’ll accept the artifacts via the shared Drive link (please upload to the folder in my ORG only). Also, can we schedule the walkthrough on Tue 2027-05-25 at 11:00 AM EDT — that works for our security and CloudOps teams.

If anything changes let me know; otherwise we’ll expect the artifact bundle and the Ops walkthrough invite.

Best,
Natalie Park

GreenBank Financial
